summary: Provision topic-aware Slack tagging + Confluence sync pipeline with archival pruner for research pods
description:
Issue summary:
We need an automated pipeline that applies topic-aware tags to newly created Slack channels for research experiment pods, syncs a lightweight metadata page in the corresponding Confluence space, and prunes/archives channels and pages that are stale based on configurable TTLs.

Impact:
- Manual tagging and doc creation is inconsistent across pods causing discovery and auditability gaps.
- Stale channels and pages accumulate, increasing noise and retention risk.
- Research and SRE spend engineering time on repetitive housekeeping.

Environment:
- Applies to all research and experiment pods in prod Slack workspace (redwood-prod).
- Confluence spaces scoped to research-pods/* namespaces.

Desired behavior / proposal:
1) On creation of a channel matching research pod pattern (e.g., pod-*-exp-*), a Slack bot should:
   - Apply topic tags based on channel description or repo metadata (topic: <ml-experiment>, <eval>, <infra>).
   - Post a stable link to the newly created Confluence stub page with the same tags in its metadata.
2) A Confluence sync function should create/update a stub page in the pod's confluence space with metadata fields: owner, start_date, tags, linked_github_repos, ttl_days.
3) A daily archival pruner job should mark channels/pages as stale and auto-archive after configurable grace period, with an opt-out label (do-not-archive).

Acceptance criteria:
- New channels under research pod naming patterns are automatically tagged within 3 minutes of creation 90% of the time.
- Confluence stub created/updated and linked to channel in 95% of observed cases.
- Archive pruner runs daily, lists candidates in a Slack #research-archive-review channel before action, and respects do-not-archive overrides.

Steps to reproduce (manual test plan):
1) Create a test channel named pod-neo-exp-043 in prod Slack.
2) Add a short description that includes keywords: eval, quant, bert.
3) Observe whether tags are applied and a Confluence stub appears within 3 minutes.
4) Set ttl_days = 7 on the Confluence stub and run the pruner job in dry-run mode to confirm it appears in review list.

Logs / diagnostic pointers:
- Slack app audit logs: https://console.slack.redwood/logs/apps/topic-bot
- Confluence creation logs: Confluence: Space Activity -> research-pods/*
- Candidate pruner output: internal S3 bucket s3://redwood-ops/research-pruner/dryrun/
